title: Why Crab Numbers Rise and Fall

scenes.tts: Every winter, survey teams tow dredges along the bottom of the Chesapeake Bay. They catch blue crabs buried in the mud. Scientists use the catches to estimate how many crabs live in the whole Bay. From one winter to the next, the estimate more than doubled. The Bay did not get bigger. So why are there lots of crabs some years, and far fewer in others?
scenes.visual: Side view of the Bay: boat tows a dredge over mud with buried crab dots; arrow to an estimate; two bars 367 and 852 million with a dashed line at twice the first; question writes in
scenes.narration: Every winter, survey teams tow dredges along the bottom of the Chesapeake Bay. They catch blue crabs buried in the mud. Scientists use the catches to estimate how many crabs live in the whole Bay. From one winter to the next, the estimate more than doubled. The Bay did not get bigger. So why are there lots of crabs some years, and far fewer in others?

scenes.tts: A population is all the members of one species living in the same place. The blue crabs in the Bay are one population. Births add crabs. So do crabs moving in. Deaths take crabs away. So do crabs moving out. When more are added than lost, the population grows. When more are lost, it shrinks.
scenes.visual: Bay outline with crab dots; blue arrows in labelled births and move in, red arrows out labelled deaths and move out; dots are added then removed
scenes.narration: A population is all the members of one species living in the same place. The blue crabs in the Bay are one population. Births add crabs. So do crabs moving in. Deaths take crabs away. So do crabs moving out. When more are added than lost, the population grows. When more are lost, it shrinks.

scenes.tts: A limiting factor is anything that keeps a population from growing larger. A biotic factor is a living part of the environment. Big crabs eat many young crabs. An abiotic factor is a nonliving part. In a very cold winter, more crabs die before spring.
scenes.visual: Two columns: biotic with a big crab and young crabs, abiotic with a very cold winter and crabs fading
scenes.narration: A limiting factor is anything that keeps a population from growing larger. A biotic factor is a living part of the environment. Big crabs eat many young crabs. An abiotic factor is a nonliving part. In a very cold winter, more crabs die before spring.

scenes.tts: Young crabs can hide from big crabs in shallow water and grass. With less grass, more young crabs need the same hiding places. That need is called competition. When a limiting factor changes, the population can change too.
scenes.visual: Three grass patches with young crabs; two patches removed and crabs crowd into one; competition label; closing line
scenes.narration: Young crabs can hide from big crabs in shallow water and grass. With less grass, more young crabs need the same hiding places. That need is called competition. When a limiting factor changes, the population can change too.

scenes.tts: Some causes are natural, like cold winters and floods. People cause changes too. One is pollution. Another is hard shorelines, which can shrink the shallow water where young crabs hide. A third is overharvesting. That means people catch a species faster than it can replace itself.
scenes.visual: Natural column and people column with chips, overharvesting defined
scenes.narration: Some causes are natural, like cold winters and floods. People cause changes too. One is pollution. Another is hard shorelines, which can shrink the shallow water where young crabs hide. A third is overharvesting. That means people catch a species faster than it can replace itself.

scenes.tts: In 2008, Virginia and Maryland made a plan. They would catch about thirty-four percent fewer female crabs than the earlier average. Females carry the eggs, so leaving more of them can mean more young crabs later. It is not a sure thing. Taking only as many as a population can replace is sustainable harvest. But a limit is not a promise, and rebuilding can take years. So why does the Bay have lots of crabs some years and few in others? The things that limit crabs keep changing.
